subject: Spatial mixture multiscale models in R-INLA?

messages.author: daf010f89f87d673
messages.subject: Spatial mixture multiscale models in R-INLA?
parts:
Hi,

I'm interested in running a spatial multiscale mixture model which accommodates for a scale effect by sharing both CH and UH simultaneously following the work by Aregay et al  (model 4 in https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/26923178 ). Aregay used WinBUGS to specify their model. My data are areal data with ~3400 clinics, nested in ~250 subdistricts. Running the Aregay model in BUGS will take an enormous amount of processing time, if it is even possible. So is it possible to run a similar model to that of Aregay using R-INLA? If so, I would be grateful for any suggestions of examples/papers/tutorials which may be helpful in specifying the model in INLA? I'm fairly new to INLA.

Alternatively is it possible to run a multiscale BYM2 model with PC priors in INLA? If so, any examples/suggestions would once again be appreciated.

Regards,
Harry

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial mixture multiscale models in R-INLA?
parts:
Hi Harry,

If I read the referred paper correctly, there is a
p*v term in the predictor, where both p and v are indexed over the regions. INLA cannot deal with the multiplication of 2 random effects of high dimension. One of them would have to be dimension 1-5 for this to work.

I think the proposed models would work if there was only one "p" for each y-variable (p same over the index).

There are of course many other possibilities for modeling regions and sub-regions in INLA. BYM2 would be one type of model component you could use for one or both levels.

I don't have any BYM2 examples myself, but look at the online resources and at the BYM paper(s) (and ask the authors).

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
